headline: Kai, earnings season hits full speed this morning with Brent at a five-month high and the ten-year holding above 5 percent.
subline: Netflix, GM and GE Aerospace report today, September housing starts land at 8:30 AM ET, and bitcoin is — for once — quiet near $82,000.
asof: Pre-market · overnight and early-morning quotes · index figures are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures idle after Monday's chip-led rebound
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures sat near 7,748 overnight after chipmakers snapped an eight-session slide — Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom all rose — while oil eased in Asia on Trump's partial waiver of Russia-energy sanctions, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Monday's rebound puts the S&P 500 at 7,690.73
items.sentence: The index rose 0.4 percent while the Nasdaq added 1.1 percent and the Dow slipped 36 points, recovering part of last week's tech-led drop, per the AP via Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Netflix leads a stacked earnings Tuesday
items.sentence: Netflix, GM, GE Aerospace, 3M and RTX report today, September housing starts land at 8:30 AM ET, and markets price only about a 15 percent chance of a Fed hike at next week's meeting, per Benzinga.

items.title: Brent sits near $110 with Hormuz still tight
items.sentence: Persian Gulf oil flows are running at about 80 percent of pre-war levels as Iran tightens its grip on the strait, keeping Brent near a five-month high, per Saxo Bank's morning take.

items.title: Bitcoin coils between its moving averages
items.sentence: It traded at $81,993 this morning, 6 percent below its October 2 high of $87,229 and just above the 50-day line at $81,481, with three straight days of unusually narrow ranges, per CryptoTicker.

items.title: France extends curfews to Nice, Lyon and Gironde
items.sentence: Overnight curfews spread beyond Paris after a weekend of rioting and looting, while Macron rejected his interior minister's offer to resign, per Anadolu Agency and the 10 Things briefing.

items.title: A Hormuz tanker attack tests the US-Iran truce
items.sentence: An attack that damaged a vessel in the strait is straining the ceasefire that ended the February war and promised commercial ships 60 days of safe passage, per AP coverage.

items.title: Trump's approval falls to 31 percent before midterms
items.sentence: Reuters/Ipsos puts him at a term low with Democrats ahead by 12 points on the generic congressional ballot two weeks from November 3, per the 10 Things briefing.

items.title: Houthi missile strike kills 53 recruits in Shabwa
items.sentence: Three ballistic missiles hit a training camp near Ataq, killing at least 53 and wounding more than 200, as fighting escalates around the Bab al-Mandab strait, per the 10 Things briefing.

items.title: Alberta votes three-to-one to stay in Canada
items.sentence: CBC projected 76.2 percent support for remaining in Canada in the nonbinding separation referendum, with about 1.36 million early and special ballots cast, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: OpenAI accelerates toward a $1.4 trillion valuation
items.sentence: The company is reportedly seeking at least $30 billion in new funding at a valuation around $1.4 trillion, per Pulse2.

items.title: AI agents ran a hundred-company breach campaign
items.sentence: A Chinese-speaking hacker reportedly deployed Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI agents in a cyberattack spanning roughly 100 companies, per OODA Loop.

items.title: AlphaGo's co-creator starts a London reasoning lab
items.sentence: Thore Graepel's Metis Reasoning is reportedly raising tens of millions to build compute-efficient, verifiable alternatives to frontier models, per Tech.eu.

items.title: Meta opens the doors on Prometheus
items.sentence: The company published an inside look at its gigawatt-scale Ohio supercluster, which trains the Muse model family and is still expanding, per The Neuron.

items.title: Canadian publishers sue Anthropic over training data
items.sentence: A coalition including Postmedia and The Globe and Mail filed suit in Ontario alleging Claude was trained on their content without permission, per The Neuron.
